'''Andrea Sella''' (born February 1961) is a chemist and broadcaster based at [[University College London]] where he is a Professor of Inorganic Chemistry.

He studies [[rare-earth metals]]<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.bbc.co.uk/programmes/b01mk1zd |title=BBC Radio 4 - The Life Scientific, Andrea Sella |publisher=Bbc.co.uk |date=2012-09-11 |accessdate=2014-08-15}}</ref>  and collaborates with several research groups on hydrogen storage, carbonitrides, and nanotube insertion chemistry. He has been involved in numerous television documentaries, including the 2010 BBC documentary'' [[Chemistry: A Volatile History]]'', which was nominated for the 2010 [[British Academy Television Awards]] in the category Specialist Factual.<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://www.imdb.com/name/nm3076136/|title=Andrea Sella|website=[[IMDb]] }}</ref> In 2014 he presented "My Family and other Ibex"<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://www.bbc.co.uk/programmes/b04gypsg|title = BBC Radio 4 Extra - My Family and Other Ibex}}</ref> and "Urine Trouble: What's in our Water"<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://www.bbc.co.uk/programmes/b04g8kc9|title = BBC Radio 4 - Urine Trouble: What's in Our Water}}</ref> on BBC Radio 4. He has been a guest on Melvyn Bragg's [[In Our Time (BBC Radio 4)|In Our Time]] and appeared regularly on radio programmes like [[Start the Week]], [[Weekend (talk show)|Weekend]], [[Newshour]], the [[Today (BBC Radio 4)|Today Programme]] and the [[Infinite Monkey Cage]]. He has been consultant and contributor for the BBC World Service's series "Elemental Economics" presented by [[Justin Rowlatt]].<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.bbc.co.uk/elements |title=Elemental Economics |publisher=Bbc.co.uk |date=2015-01-23 |accessdate=2015-01-23}}</ref>

==Early life==
Sella was born in [[Milan, Italy]], in 1961, but grew up in [[New York City|New York]], USA, and [[Nairobi, Kenya]].

He studied chemistry at [[Trinity College, Toronto|Trinity College]], University of Toronto, as an undergraduate and started research for a PhD under Professor Robert H. Morris on [[molecular hydrogen]] compounds. He obtained a D.Phil. in Chemistry from 1986–1990 at [[Balliol College, Oxford]] studying with Professor [[Malcolm Green (chemist)|Malcolm Green]].

==Career==
Sella was appointed Lecturer at [[University College London|UCL]] in 1990. He was awarded an [[EPSRC]] Senior Media Fellowship from 2007 to 2012. He was promoted to Professor in 2012. His research interests include the molecular chemistry of the lanthanides, the confinement of elemental phosphorus inside carbon nanotubes, and the synthesis and properties of layered carbonitrides.

His monthly column in the Royal Society of Chemistry's [[Chemistry World]], "Classic Kit", with guest contributions by his Masters student, Talitha Humphrey and others, explores the history of chemistry through the lens of scientific apparatus.<ref>{{cite web |url=https://sellathechemist.wordpress.com/classic-kit-chemical-apparatus-with-a-name/ |title=Classic Kit &#124; Chemistry World |date=June 2010 |publisher=Rsc.org |accessdate=2022-03-28 }}</ref>

He is also well known for science demonstrations for both school children and adults.<ref>{{cite web|author=Nina Notman |url=http://www.rsc.org/chemistryworld/2012/10/science-communication-andrea-sella |title=Pied Piper of chemistry &#124; Chemistry World |publisher=Rsc.org |date= |accessdate=2014-08-15}}</ref> He sits on the Scientific Advisory Board of the [[Cheltenham Science Festival]].

He was awarded the 2014 [[Michael Faraday Prize]] from the [[Royal Society]] for "his excellent work in science communication".<ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.ucl.ac.uk/news/news-articles/0814/050814-royal-society |title=UCL scientists honoured by Royal Society|publisher=University College London |date=2014-08-24}}</ref>

Since February 2014, he has been a frequent guest speaker in a [[BBC World Service]] radio programme called "''Elements''".<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://www.bbc.co.uk/programmes/p01rcrn6|title=Elements - BBC World Service|website=BBC|access-date=2016-09-18}}</ref> He explains how [[chemical element]]s behave, react, and how they are used. In the programme that aired on 16 September 2016 featuring [[thorium]], he temporarily replaced [[Justin Rowlatt]] as the host.<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://www.bbc.co.uk/programmes/p04838xg|title=Thorium (Th), Elements - BBC World Service|website=BBC|access-date=2016-09-18}}</ref>

He has also presented several programmes on BBC Radio 4 and [[BBC World Service]].

Sella returned his [[Michael Faraday Prize]] in June 2025 over the [[Royal Society]]'s "failure to take stronger action against [[Elon Musk]], a fellow of the UK academy, for presiding over 'onslaughts on US science."<ref>{{cite news|title=Royal Society prize winner returns award in protest over Elon Musk|url=https://www.ft.com/content/877853df-1687-4d1f-940b-9eefc0cf69c0|access-date=10 June 2025|work=Financial Times|date=10 June 2025|archive-date=10 June 2025|archive-url=https://archive.today/20250610040921/https://www.ft.com/content/877853df-1687-4d1f-940b-9eefc0cf69c0#selection-1587.0-1587.66|url-status=live}}</ref>
